original_value: This paper investigates extreme multistability and its controllability for an ideal voltage‐controlled memristor emulator‐based canonical Chua’s circuit. With the voltage‐current model, the initial condition‐dependent extreme multistability is explored through analyzing the stability distribution of line equilibrium point and then the coexisting infinitely many attractors are numerically uncovered in such a memristive circuit by the attraction basin and phase portraits. Furthermore, based on the accurate constitutive relation of the memristor emulator, a set of incremental flux‐charge describing equations for the memristor‐based canonical Chua’s circuit are formulated and a dimensionality reduction model is thus established. As a result, the initial condition‐dependent dynamics in the voltage‐current domain is converted into the system parameter‐associated dynamics in the flux‐charge domain, which is confirmed by numerical simulations and circuit simulations. Therefore, a controllable strategy for extreme multistability can be expediently implemented, which is greatly significant for seeking chaos‐based engineering applications of multistable memristive circuits.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines extreme multistability and its controllability in an ideal voltage-controlled memristor emulator-based canonical Chua’s circuit. Using the voltage-current model, it investigates initial-condition-dependent extreme multistability by analyzing the stability distribution of line equilibrium points, then numerically reveals the coexisting infinitely many attractors in this memristive circuit through attraction basins and phase portraits. In addition, based on the precise constitutive relation of the memristor emulator, a set of incremental flux-charge describing equations for the memristor-based canonical Chua’s circuit is established and a reduced-dimensional model is constructed. Consequently, the initial-condition-dependent dynamics in the voltage-current domain are transformed into system-parameter-associated dynamics in the flux-charge domain, as verified by numerical and circuit simulations. Thus, an expedient control strategy for extreme multistability can be implemented, which is highly important for exploring chaos-based engineering applications of multistable memristive circuits.
